config.title: Build form state manager from scratch

intro.title: Build form state manager from scratch
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form state manager from scratch using plain JavaScript. You'll learn how to create a reusable function that tracks and updates form input values in real-time. The core concept involves using JavaScript objects to store state and event listeners to handle user interactions. By the end, you'll have a working state manager that can manage multiple form fields efficiently.
intro.usecase: Form state management is essential in any application that collects user input, from simple contact forms on websites to complex multi-step registration flows in banking apps. Developers implement this pattern in e-commerce checkout processes, where shipping details, payment information, and order summaries must be tracked and validated. In enterprise software like CRM systems, form state managers handle dynamic fields for customer data entry while maintaining validation rules. This foundational skill enables you to build responsive, user-friendly interfaces that prevent data loss and provide immediate feedback.

objectives: Initialize a form state object with multiple input fields
Implement an event handler to update form state on user input
Bind form input elements to the state object using JavaScript
Construct a validation function to check form field requirements
Render dynamic feedback based on validation results
Reset the form state to its initial values
Integrate form submission with state management logic

steps.title: Create the form state manager function
steps.instruction: Create a function called createFormState that will serve as our form state manager. The function should be empty for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure to name it exactly 'createFormState'.
steps.seedCode: // Create the form state manager function
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a function named createFormState defined in your code.
successCriteria: The createFormState function is defined with the correct name.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined a function named createFormState.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to create a function called createFormState.

steps.title: Initialize form state object
steps.instruction: Inside the createFormState function, initialize a state object with 'values' and 'errors' properties, both set to empty objects.
steps.hint: You can create an object with properties values and errors, each initialized as an empty object {}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createFormState function should now contain an initialized state object with values and errors properties.
successCriteria: A state object with properties values and errors is initialized inside createFormState.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both 'values' and 'errors' properties are included and set to empty objects.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state object initialization is missing or incorrect. Ensure you create an object with both 'values' and 'errors' properties.

steps.title: Add getState method
steps.instruction: Inside the createFormState function, add a getState method that returns the current state object.
steps.hint: Add a method to the function that returns the state variable you initialized earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createFormState function will have a getState method that returns the current state object.
successCriteria: The getState method is defined inside createFormState and returns the state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but make sure it returns the state variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The getState method is missing or doesn't return the state object.

steps.title: Add resetForm method
steps.instruction: Add a resetForm method inside the createFormState function that clears all field values and errors.
steps.hint: The method should reset the state object to its initial empty structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createFormState function will have a resetForm method that can clear the form state.
successCriteria: A resetForm method is added inside createFormState that resets the state object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a method, but make sure it's named resetForm and resets the state object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The resetForm method is missing or incorrectly implemented.

steps.title: Create example form structure
steps.instruction: Create a simple HTML form with name and email fields to demonstrate the state manager
steps.hint: Add a <form> element with two <input> fields inside - one for name and one for email. You can add labels and a submit button too.
steps.expectedOutcome: A basic HTML form with name and email fields will be created to test the form state manager.
successCriteria: The code includes a form element with at least two input fields (name and email)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating a form, but make sure to include both name and email input fields inside the form element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form structure isn't quite right. You need to create a form element with input fields for name and email.

steps.title: Initialize form state manager instance
steps.instruction: Create an instance of your createFormState function and assign it to a variable called formManager.
steps.hint: Call the function like you would any other function and store the returned object in a variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating an instance of a function that returns an object
const calculator = createCalculator();
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a formManager variable that holds the form state manager instance.
successCriteria: formManager variable is declared and assigned the result of calling createFormState()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling createFormState() and storing the result in a variable named formManager.
steps.feedbackWrong: create an instance of createFormState and store it in a formManager variable.

steps.title: Wire form events to state manager
steps.instruction: Add event listeners to the form inputs that call the updateField and validateField methods on the form manager instance when values change.
steps.hint: Use the onchange or oninput event on each input element to call the appropriate methods with the field name and new value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The form inputs will now update the form state and trigger validation whenever their values change.
successCriteria: Both name and email inputs have event listeners that call updateField and validateField with the correct field names and values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some event listeners, but make sure both inputs are wired and both updateField and validateField are called.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form inputs are not properly connected to the state manager. Check that each input has an event listener that calls both updateField and validateField.
